clue.text: Destroyer in a lake overlooked by spit

indicators.note: what is overlooked is passed over and left out, so those letters drop from the word

parts.note: spit is saliva
taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A warship lurking in a lake, hidden behind a sandy spit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroyer' and 'spit' both suggest the sea and the shore; take A and L out of SALIVA to leave SIVA.
explanation.definitionFit: Siva (Shiva) is the Hindu god whose role in the trinity is the destruction of the universe.

clue.text: Such is zloty, pay with secondary deductions leads to mild disorder

indicators.note: secondary deductions are subtractions of the second item, so each word loses its second letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that being paid in Polish currency is enough to make anyone a little unhinged.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the second letter of each of the four words: S(U)CH, I(S), Z(L)OTY, P(A)Y, giving SCHIZOTYPY.
explanation.definitionFit: Schizotypy is a personality trait describing milder, subclinical versions of the features seen in schizophrenia.

clue.text: Examination to check stray civet

indicators.note: to check something is to hold it back, so one word is held inside the other

parts.note: a viva is an oral examination at university
to stray is to err

explanation.surface: A vet examines a stray civet cat that has wandered in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stray' reads as an adjective describing the civet, but it is a verb meaning err, which goes inside VIVA.
explanation.definitionFit: Viverra is the zoological genus containing the typical civets of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Scot's variation in complexion if recently perplexed

indicators.note: something perplexed is confused and muddled, so these letters are jumbled up

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters

explanation.surface: A Scotsman puzzled by a recent change in his skin tone.
explanation.definitionFit: A fernytickle is the Scots word for a freckle, a small spot that varies the colour of the skin.

clue.text: Performed badly, cut up about pet, one producing stink

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the other letters are placed around the rest
in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top
cutting a word trims its tail, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: to muff something is to perform it badly
luv is an informal term of endearment, like pet
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who botched a job and is upset about a pet that makes a terrible smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' is not an animal but a British term of endearment; 'cut' and 'up' both act on the botched performance before it wraps around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An effluvium is an unpleasant smell or exhalation given off by something, so a stench.

clue.text: Turn weak, entering constant darkness up north

indicators.note: to turn the word around is to read its letters backwards
something entering goes inside, so one letter is placed within the others

parts.note: weak, as of a drink, is thin
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: Feeling faint as perpetual darkness falls in the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: THIN read backwards is NIHT, and C goes inside it. 'Up north' marks a Scottish word rather than a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicht is the Scots form of night, the dark part of the day, and Scotland is the north of Britain.

clue.text: Short slip with US volume on radical Islam's Semitic feature

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the pieces follow one another
a short version of a word is clipped, losing its final letter

parts.note: a slip or stumble is a trip
liter is the American spelling of litre, a unit of volume

indicators.note: a radical change is a thorough rearrangement, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the word itself, without the possessive

explanation.surface: Political talk about a slip-up involving an American and radical Islam.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Islam’s is the possessive that joins wordplay to definition; only ISLAM is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Triliteralism is the characteristic of Semitic languages such as Hebrew and Arabic that most word roots have three consonants.

clue.text: "Vital energy connected to river/sea", local tweeted

parts.note: chi is the vital life force in Chinese philosophy
R is the abbreviation for river
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A local resident posts an online message about energy connecting rivers and the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweeted' suggests social media, but here it is the birdsong sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To chirm is a dialect verb for birds chirping or warbling, so chirmed means made a bird's twittering call.

clue.text: Top-to-bottom change in personality needed for Shakespearean tangles

indicators.note: in a down entry, moving the top letter to the bottom shifts the first letter to the end

parts.note: one's personality is one's self

explanation.surface: A complete personality transformation required to perform Shakespeare's knotty passages.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare, to elf hair is to mat or knot it, as Edgar does in King Lear, so elfs means tangles as a verb.

clue.text: Partially privatise hospital conception system, getting around contrary opponent

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: getting around means encircling, so these letters surround the next piece

parts.note: IVF, in vitro fertilisation, is a method of achieving conception

indicators.note: contrary means facing the opposite way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an opponent is a foe

explanation.surface: A health service selling off its fertility unit despite opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conception system' reads like a design concept, but it is the fertility treatment; the reversed opponent sits inside it, not after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hive off is to separate part of an organisation, often by selling it to private owners.

clue.text: Safe inversion of Sondheim show?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: no longer in danger
second meaning: the opposite of the musical Into the Woods, swapping into for its opposite

explanation.walkthrough: Sondheim's musical is Into the Woods; inverting into gives the idiom for being past danger, which the question mark flags as a playful second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes having escaped trouble or danger, so someone in that position is safe.

clue.text: The creature I spotted in greasy spoon was a louse

indicators.note: spotted in means seen inside a place, so these letters sit within another word

parts.note: a caff is a cheap British café, a greasy spoon
a creature of unknown kind may be called it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone spotted at a grotty café turned out to be a low character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Louse' looks like an insect, but it means a contemptible person. Caff is British slang for a cheap café.
explanation.definitionFit: A caitiff is an archaic word for a base, cowardly wretch, the same as calling someone a louse.

clue.text: Faith in Spanish retailer of clothing, so svelte with small inset

indicators.note: something inset is set into the middle of something else

parts.note: Zara is the Spanish fashion chain
so means thus
svelte means slim or trim
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Trusting in a Spanish clothes shop to make you slim, with a small size tucked in.
explanation.walkthrough: The small inset applies only to the svelte word, not to the whole answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Zarathustrism is Zoroastrianism, the ancient Persian religion named after its prophet Zarathustra.

clue.text: Experiencing pain when wearing undergarment with raised boundary and short line of symmetry

indicators.note: a word wearing a garment is enclosed by it, so it sits inside

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment
achy means hurting

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted up, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: in cricket a ball cleared over the boundary scores six, and the shot itself is called a boundary

explanation.surface: A tight undergarment chafing along its edge.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a six is a hit that clears the boundary rope on the full, so a boundary can stand for six.
explanation.definitionFit: The brachyaxis is the shorter lateral axis of a crystal, a line about which it is symmetrical.

clue.text: Platter with food originally banned in strict diet

parts.note: a platter is a tray

indicators.note: originally points to the origin, the very first letter of the word

parts.note: first letter of food

explanation.surface: A platter of food that a strict dieter is not allowed to touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Trayf (treif) describes food that is not kosher and so forbidden under Jewish dietary law.

clue.text: One rarely takes action against head demon?

parts.note: an imp is a little demon
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: Seldom does anyone take on the chief of the devils.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are taken in reverse of the clue's order: a head demon is an IMP LEADER.
explanation.definitionFit: An impleader is one who brings a lawsuit, an old legal term for a plaintiff suing someone.

clue.text: Composition of doggerel from Old French and in Danish, say

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these letters go within another word

parts.note: a Danish is a pastry
O is the abbreviation for old
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: A piece of bad verse taken from Old French and Danish sources.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old French' looks like a language, but it splits into O and the French ET; 'Danish' is the pastry, not the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetastry is the work of a poetaster, an inferior poet who writes trivial or worthless verse.

clue.text: Strait-laced person adopts uncertain expression to hold over French conciliator

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the outer word takes other letters inside it

parts.note: a prude is a prim, strait-laced person

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so one letter sits inside

parts.note: hmm is a noise of doubt
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A prim person takes on a doubtful tone in mediating a French dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions nest: over goes into the doubtful noise, and that whole piece goes into the strait-laced person. O for over comes from cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A prud'homme is a member of a French industrial tribunal that settles disputes between employers and workers.

clue.text: Fresh university location for Newark and even parts of Land's End

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university
Newark is in New Jersey, abbreviated NJ

indicators.note: even parts are the letters in positions two, four, six and so on

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of LANDSEND

explanation.surface: A new university sited somewhere between Newark and the far tip of Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost point of mainland England, in Cornwall; only its even letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Unjaded means not worn out or dulled by overuse, so still fresh and lively.

clue.text: Classically elegant trellis with sides lopped

indicators.note: lopping the sides cuts off both edges, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: a trellis is a lattice

explanation.surface: Pruning the edges of a garden trellis for a neat, classical look.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic describes the refined, pure style of ancient Athens, used for elegant classical taste.

clue.text: UK right to spaff money overseas

indicators.note: to spaff is a slang word for squandering or splashing about, so these letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Britain claims an entitlement to fritter cash abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The tughrik (tugrik) is the currency of Mongolia, so it is money in a foreign land.

clue.text: Weber composed Erika with discordant framing in unspeakable style?

indicators.note: a frame surrounds a picture, so this word goes around the rest
something composed is put together in a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a discordant sound is jangly
Wb is the symbol for the weber, the unit of magnetic flux

explanation.surface: The composer Weber wrote a harsh, jarring piece called Erika that is painful to listen to.
explanation.walkthrough: Weber looks like the composer but is the unit, symbol Wb; WB plus ERIKA is rearranged and placed inside JANGLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawbreakingly describes words so hard to say they might break your jaw, hence almost impossible to pronounce.

clue.text: No end of interest in payment for use of an organ

indicators.note: no means without, so the chosen letter is taken away

parts.note: rental is a payment for the use of something

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of interest

explanation.surface: Paying a fee to hire a church organ, with no interest charged.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal means relating to the kidneys, which are organs of the body.

clue.text: Perth's wet weather in which spirits must be kept up

indicators.note: in a down clue, keeping something up means reading it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: rums are spirits

explanation.surface: In rainy Perth you need to keep your spirits up.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth here is the Scottish city, signalling a Scots word; 'spirits kept up' sounds like morale but is drinks turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Smur is a Scots word for a fine drizzling rain, typical of the weather in Scotland.

clue.text: Yoghurty drink US hacker smuggled into satellite

indicators.note: something smuggled into a place is hidden inside it

parts.note: the moon is Earth's satellite
adz is the American spelling of adze, a cutting tool used for hacking wood

explanation.surface: An American computer hacker sneaks a yoghurt drink onto a satellite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hacker' suggests a computer criminal, but here it is a tool that hacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Madzoon (matzoon) is a fermented milk product from Armenia, a yoghurt-like drink.

clue.text: Beside Devon river, nine shrubs needing little water

indicators.note: beside means placed next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: the Tamar is the river forming the border between Devon and Cornwall
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Nine bushes growing by a river in Devon that need hardly any watering.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamarix is the genus of tamarisks, shrubs adapted to dry and salty ground that tolerate drought.

clue.text: Sets out anew, going over mountain face in second year

indicators.note: going over suggests flipping right round, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these letters sit within the following word

parts.note: YR is the abbreviation for year
an alp is a mountain
a face, as of a cliff, is a side

explanation.surface: A climber puts on a new show, tackling a mountain's face in their second year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going over' looks like it means about or again, matching the RE- of the answer, but it reverses the whole wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To redisplay is to arrange or exhibit again, so redisplays means puts on show once more.

clue.text: Men from S Africa's classic race given voice

indicators.note: given voice means spoken out loud, so the answer is how the word sounds

parts.note: the Oaks is one of the five English classic horse races, run at Epsom

explanation.surface: South African men talking about a famous horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oaks is a British flat race for fillies, one of the five Classics.
explanation.definitionFit: Oke is South African slang for a man or a bloke, so okes are guys there.
